Bitcoin shrugged it off, ending the US session near $65,150 on Kraken, up from about $64,650 at the afternoon edition.

briefing.changed: Stocks got worse after the afternoon edition: the Nasdaq slide deepened from about 2% to a 2.3% close and Nvidia's loss doubled. Bitcoin did not follow and edged up about $500, and Zcash recovered to about $900. Fed Chair Warsh said nothing about interest rates.
briefing.question: Will bitcoin keep decoupling from tech shares if Nvidia's results on Tuesday night disappoint?
briefing.watch: US retail sales on Tuesday at 13:30 UK, then Nvidia's results after the US close, about 21:20 UK. The next 🔴 event is the Fed decision on Wednesday 9 December at 19:00 UK.

lead.headline: Bitcoin holds firm as Wall Street's AI sell-off deepens into the close
lead.standfirst: The Nasdaq closed down 2.3% and Nvidia lost about 4% before its results, but bitcoin ended the US session slightly higher near $65,150.
body: US stocks closed sharply lower on Monday as the sell-off in artificial intelligence shares deepened through the afternoon. The Nasdaq Composite fell 2.30% to 24,556.89, the S&P 500 lost 1.78% and the Dow fell 1.26%, according to Reuters figures published by the Korea Times.

Nvidia fell about 4.2% the day before its third-quarter results, its first since Jensen Huang stepped down as chief executive. Anthropic's planned stock market debut later this week added to the focus on AI valuations.
Bitcoin did not follow shares lower. It traded near $65,150 on Kraken at 21:30 UK, up from about $64,650 at the afternoon edition, and stayed inside the day's range of roughly $63,840 to $65,630.

Strategy said in a filing that it bought 485 bitcoin between 9 and 15 November for about $33.4 million, at an average of $68,887, The Block reported. It also spent $228.1 million buying back STRC preferred shares.

Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's remarks at the San Francisco Fed were about AI and productivity and did not address interest rates. Spot bitcoin ETF flows for Monday were not yet published at the time of writing.

headline: The Nasdaq closed down 2.3% and Nvidia lost about 4% before Tuesday's results, but bitcoin edged up to about $65,150. Strategy kept buying, and Warsh stayed silent on rates.
spoken: Cryptonaire Post, evening edition. Wall Street closed sharply lower, with the Nasdaq down about two point three percent and Nvidia down about four percent, a day before its results. Bitcoin held up, ending the US session near sixty-five thousand one hundred and fifty dollars, slightly higher than this afternoon. Strategy said it bought four hundred and eighty-five bitcoin last week. Fed Chair Warsh spoke about artificial intelligence, not interest rates. Zcash recovered to about nine hundred dollars. Tomorrow, US retail sales at half past one, then Nvidia's results at about twenty past nine in the evening, UK time. Information only, not advice.

stories.title: Nasdaq closes down 2.3% as Nvidia slides before results
stories.why: The sell-off deepened after the afternoon edition: the Nasdaq closed down 2.30%, the S&P 500 down 1.78% and the Dow down 1.26%, per Reuters figures in the Korea Times. Nvidia fell about 4.2% ahead of Tuesday night's results, double its loss at the afternoon edition.
stories.caveat: TipRanks reported slightly bigger falls (Nasdaq -2.49%, S&P 500 -1.91%, Nvidia -5%); final figures may differ by a few tenths.

note.read: AI shares are being de-risked hard into Nvidia's results and Anthropic's debut, which keeps pressure on wider risk appetite.
note.alt: Heavy positioning before a known event can reverse quickly once the results are out.
note.change: A solid Nvidia report and a Nasdaq rebound on Wednesday would ease this pressure.

stories.title: Bitcoin edges up to $65,150 despite the stock slide
stories.why: Bitcoin stood near $65,150 on Kraken at 21:30 UK, up from about $64,650 at the afternoon edition, inside a day range of about $63,840 to $65,630. It failed to hold $65,000 around the US open, Cointelegraph reported, but recovered later even as the Nasdaq fell further. The 200-week average sits near $68,200, per Cointelegraph.

note.read: The afternoon worry that bitcoin was lagging and would catch down did not play out; the selling today stayed in shares.
note.alt: Thin evening trading can flatter the price; the real test is Nvidia on Tuesday night.
note.change: A drop through the day's low near $63,840, or a large ETF outflow figure for Monday.

stories.title: Strategy buys 485 BTC and $228m of its own preferred shares
stories.why: Strategy bought 485 BTC for about $33.4 million between 9 and 15 November at an average of $68,887, taking holdings to 850,849 BTC at an average cost of $75,452, The Block reported from its 8-K filing. It spent far more, $228.1 million, buying back STRC preferred shares. At today's price its holdings are below cost.

stories.title: Warsh speaks on AI, says nothing on rates
stories.why: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's opening remarks at the San Francisco Fed covered AI and productivity, setting out staff scenarios from broad gains to a disappointment where AI returns fall and equity valuations drop. He gave no signal on interest rates ahead of the 9 December decision.

stories.title: Zcash recovers to about $900
stories.why: Zcash traded near $901 on Kraken at 21:30 UK, up from about $883 at the afternoon edition and well off the day's low near $846 as the grants vote opened. It is still slightly below where it opened the day, near $915.

stories.title: Lighter halts withdrawals after $10.4m theft
stories.why: Perpetual futures exchange Lighter paused all withdrawals after about $10.4 million was taken using one trader's leaked API key, CoinDesk reported; it says its contracts were not compromised. Part of the funds were routed to Hyperliquid. Another reminder of venue risk in a fearful market.
stories.caveat: Some researchers put losses at $15.5 million; Lighter has not confirmed that.

stories.title: Supreme Court ends Custodia's fight for a Fed account
stories.why: The US Supreme Court declined to hear Custodia Bank's case, leaving the Fed free to refuse master accounts to crypto banks, The Block reported. The Fed has proposed a limited 'skinny' account instead; Kraken's bank won a full one in March.

explained.title: Why Strategy's average cost matters
body: Strategy has bought bitcoin at an average of about $75,450 each. With bitcoin near $65,000, its holdings are worth less than it paid, a paper loss of several billion dollars.

That matters because the company raises money through shares and preferred stock to buy bitcoin. When the coin trades below its cost, that funding gets harder, which is why its weekly purchases have shrunk and why it is now spending more on buying back preferred shares than on bitcoin.

investigating: Did ETF outflows run to an eighth day on Monday? Evidence: Farside and SoSoValue figures, due overnight.
Is bitcoin genuinely decoupling from tech shares? Evidence: how it trades through Nvidia's results on Tuesday night.
